---
title: "Getting started"
---

## Install

ggpclient needs R 4.1 or later.

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jossl95/ggpclientR")
```

Downloading, unpacking and preprocessing run in background R processes ([mirai](https://mirai.r-lib.org)) that load the
installed package, so install it rather than only `devtools::load_all()`-ing it.

## Log in

Downloading needs the access link the portal e-mails you (request it on the portal's login page). The link is valid
for seven days and works like a password, so it is only asked for: there is no environment variable for it, and it is
never stored or logged.

```r
p <- ggp_client()
p |> ggp_login()      # asks you to paste the link; the input is hidden
```

The session is saved in `data/.session.json` (readable only by you) and reused, so the link is needed once. ggpclient
looks for a login in this order:

1. the saved session, if it still works (also one made by the Python package, which uses the same file);
2. the `access_url` argument of `ggp_client()`, for scripts that cannot ask;
3. otherwise it asks (input hidden, needs the askpass package). With no terminal to ask on it stops with an error of
   class `ggp_login_error`.

::: {.callout-warning}
Do not type the link in a script: it stays in your history. Syncing and downloading log in by themselves when needed.
:::

## Index the portal

```r
p <- ggp_client()
p |> ggp_sync()                         # all datasets into data/catalogue.sqlite
ggp_rows(p)                             # one row per file
```

`ggp_sync()` reads the public dataset pages, then logs in to add the Harmonized Histories and Additional Datasets, which
the portal lists only on the logged-in data access page. Without a login it indexes the rest and says what it skipped.

## Filters

The filters go into `ggp_client()` and apply to every step. Each takes one value, several, or nothing (all). Case does
not matter, and a value that is not in the catalogue is an error, not an empty result.

| filter | values |
|---|---|
| `project` | `"ggs"`, `"ffs"`, `"hh"` (Harmonized Histories), `"other"` (Additional Datasets), `"teaching"` |
| `round` | `1`, `2` (or `"i"`, `"ii"`) |
| `wave` | `"w1"`, `"w2"`, `"pilot"`, ...; for `hh` and `other` the dataset name, e.g. `"nkps"` |
| `country` | two-letter codes: `"nl"`, `"at"`, ... |
| `ids` | catalogue ids and ranges: `"3-12,20"` |
| `all_versions` | `TRUE` also gives superseded versions (default: the latest only) |

```r
p <- ggp_client(project = "ggs", round = 2, country = c("nl", "at"))
ggp_rows(p)      # look first: this is what the steps will work on
```

## Download

```r
p |> ggp_download(ext = "dta")          # done, skipped, failed
```

`ext` is the datafile type(s) to keep: `"dta"`, `"sav"`, `"rds"`, `"csv"`, several, or none for dta, sav and csv.
`metadata = TRUE` also keeps documentation and codebooks. Files go to `data/download/raw`, in lower-case folders.
Existing files are never overwritten unless the client was made with `force = TRUE`; a file already unpacked for these
options is skipped. A transfer is checked and tried again when it is cut short.
Each step returns a result that prints as `download: 5 done, 2 skipped, 0 failed` and lists the failures.

## In the background

`ggp_download()`, `ggp_preprocess()`, `ggp_consolidate()` and `ggp_stata()` take `async = TRUE`: they run in a
background process and return a mirai at once. `m <- p |> ggp_preprocess(async = TRUE)`, then `m[]` waits for the result.
Log in first: the background process uses the saved session.
